title: New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $567m over harms to children’s mental health
titleZh: 新墨西哥州法院命令 Meta 因损害儿童心理健康而支付 5.67 亿美元
author: boplicity
relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: A New Mexico court has ordered Meta, the parent company of Facebook, to pay $567m into a fund aimed at redressing adverse mental health impacts from the social media giant’s platforms.The Thursday ruling comes as a part of the second phase of a landmark trial the social media giant lost in March. At the time, a jury found that the company knowingly harmed children’s mental health and concealed what it knew about child sexual exploitation on its platforms, and imposed the maximum penalty: a $375m fine.The ruling on Thursday is an addition to that fine, bringing the total amount Meta is responsible for to $942m.Judge Bryan Biedscheid said the bulk of the money – $420m – would be used for treatment services for young people in New Mexico. The rest will go toward awareness and prevention, screening services and other costs over the next five years.The March trial was the first to find Meta liable for acts committed on its platform, and followed a 2023 Guardian investigation that revealed how Facebook and Instagram had become marketplaces for child sex trafficking.Several former Meta moderators told the Guardian there were instances where they flagged harmful content related to child grooming, but the cases were not escalated.In the second phase of the trial, which began in May, prosecutors had asked the judge to impose fundamental changes at Meta aimed at reining in addictive features, improving age verification, and preventing child sexual exploitation through default privacy settings and closer oversight.The judge has also ordered other changes, including that Facebook and Instagram build banner and informational screens to clearly explain its protection features, best practices, and tools to address inappropriate comment.Those changes, and an educational campaign in New Mexico, would be subject to review by the state.The court said federal children’s privacy laws prevent Meta from applying age-verification tools to children under 13. The court also noted that ordering verification of children’s ages only for Meta and not other social media companies would be “inequitable and unduly injurious” to the company.Instead, the court ordered Meta to continue to improve its age-assurance tools in New Mexico, which include using artificial intelligence to determine people’s age based on signals such as who their friends are and what types of content they post and consume. Meta must also attempt to develop a dedicated “under-13-years-of-age prediction model” in the next two years.Additionally, Meta should also request proof of age for Instagram and Facebook users in New Mexico it estimates to be under 13. If it determines a user to be under 13, or under 18 but without being able to estimate a specific age, Meta must treat the user as under 13 or under 18 until the user verifies their age.The company must also partner with schools or a child safety organization to create a reporting portal where school staff can flag users who may be under 13. And it must delete personal information it has collected on users under 13. The court also ordered Meta to report on its progress twice a year on how it is complying with the abatement measures.New Mexico’s attorney general, Raúl Torrez, hailed the judgment.“This case has always been about protecting children, standing up for families, and making sure that one of the world’s largest technology companies cannot profit from practices that endanger young people without consequence,” Torrez said in a statement.“Today’s decision is a victory for every parent who has worried about what social media is doing to their child and every child who deserves to grow up safer online.”A Meta spokesperson said in a statement to the Guardian on Thursday that the company “disagrees with the ruling” and planned to appeal.“We work hard to keep people safe on our platforms and have been transparent about the challenges of identifying and removing bad actors and harmful content. We remain confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” the statement continued.The total amount Meta is responsible for is a small fraction of its annual profit, which was about $60bn in 2025. Still, it represents another setback for Meta as it faces a wave of accusations from families of children harmed by social media.The company is embroiled in a slew of lawsuits in other US states over its alleged harms to young people. In a trial in Tennessee that began last month, the state has accused the company of disregarding internal warnings about teenagers’ compulsive use of Instagram, which has been linked to eating disorders and depression, among other adverse effects. Meta is also gearing up for a trial later this month in federal court in Oakland, California.What comes out of New Mexico is the first of many dominoes that could fall for Meta, said Laura Edelson, an assistant professor at Northeastern University focusing on social media and cybersecurity.“America is not going to pass a law that bans social media,” Edelson said. “But if companies like Meta know they’re causing harm to users by product design, the states are finally finding a way to rein this in.”

comments.author: tmp10423288442
comments.textRawHtml:
A lot of people on this story are making the usual snarky remarks that, oh, this is just a slap on the wrist—some trivial proportion of Meta’s global revenue. And that is true, but unlike the EU, for example, New Mexico is a tiny jurisdiction. It only has a little bit more than 2 million people.

So actually, a fine—or a judgment—of $942 million that applies just to New Mexico is enormous. If you look at Meta’s revenue from the U.S. and Canada and assign it proportionally by population, you find that Meta only earned about $1.5 billion to $2 billion total from New Mexico over the past five years. The exact figure depends on whether you allocate purely by population or account for purchasing power, which makes the estimate a little lower because New Mexico is a poorer state than the U.S. average.

Given that, the judgment is a half to two-thirds of what Meta could have obtained from New Mexico. So it is actually a serious deterrent, assuming Meta thinks New Mexico would continue to impose fines of that size.

I also think that there’s a good chance this judgment gets overturned or significantly reduced on appeal, but even if the fine drops to half its current level, it would be proportionately larger than almost any fine against any company, let alone tech, that I’ve heard of.
comments.textZhHtml:
这篇报道中的很多人都发表了常见的尖刻评论，哦，这只是小事一桩——占 Meta 全球收入的微不足道的一部分。确实如此，但与欧盟不同的是，新墨西哥州是一个很小的司法管辖区。它只有 200 万多一点点的人口。

所以实际上，仅适用于新墨西哥州的 9.42 亿美元罚款（或判决）是巨大的。如果你看看 Meta 在美国和加拿大的收入，并按人口比例分配，你会发现过去 5 年 Meta 从新墨西哥州总共只赚了约 15 亿到 20 亿美元。确切的数字取决于你是纯粹按人口分配还是考虑购买力，这使得估计值略低，因为新墨西哥州是一个比美国平均水平更贫穷的州。

鉴于此，该判断是 Meta 可以从新墨西哥州获得的一半到三分之二。因此，假设 Meta 认为新墨西哥州将继续征收如此数额的罚款，这实际上是一种严重的威慑。

我还认为，这一判决很有可能在上诉时被推翻或大幅减少，但即使罚款降至目前水平的一半，按比例来说，它也将比我听说过的几乎任何针对任何公司的罚款都要高，更不用说科技公司了。

children.author: tristanj
children.textRawHtml:
This analysis actually understates how massive and outsized the penalties are. The court ruling only applies to children in New Mexico under age 18.

New Mexico has ~450,000 people under age 18, of which roughly 140,000 are between ages 13-17 (Meta officially requires age 13+ to use their platforms). Recent Pew surveys of U.S. teens ages 13–17 show ~70% of teenagers use Instagram and ~30% use Facebook.

In New Mexico, Instagram and Facebook would have ~100,000 users in the 13-17 group. That's not everyone, some underage users may lie about their age, so add in ~30,000 unauthorized users under age 13. Overall, around 130,000 people in the affected class.

The judge assessed $942 million in total penalties, and dividing that $942 million across 130,000 users equals approximately $7,250 in fines per user.

If this fine remains, and Meta pays out to the affected parties, these kids could end up rewarded with thousands of dollars for just for having a Facebook or Instagram account. Which creates some bizarre incentives, minors get rewarded for signing up for the platforms that are harming them in the first place.
children.textZhHtml:
这一分析实际上低估了处罚的严重程度。该法院裁决仅适用于新墨西哥州 18 岁以下的儿童。

新墨西哥州约有 450,000 名 18 岁以下人口，其中约 140,000 人年龄在 13-17 岁之间（Meta 官方要求 13 岁以上才能使用其平台）。皮尤研究中心最近对 13-17 岁美国青少年进行的调查显示，约 70% 的青少年使用 Instagram，约 30% 使用 Facebook。

在新墨西哥州，Instagram 和 Facebook 在 13-17 岁群体中拥有约 100,000 位用户。这并不是所有人的情况，一些未成年用户可能会谎报自己的年龄，因此请加上大约 30,000 名 13 岁以下的未经授权用户。总的来说，受影响的人数约为 130,000 人。

法官评估的罚款总额为 9.42 亿美元，将这 9.42 亿美元除以 130,000 名用户，等于每个用户约 7,250 美元的罚款。

如果这笔罚款仍然存在，Meta 将支付对于受影响的各方来说，这些孩子最终可能会因为拥有 Facebook 或 Instagram 帐户而获得数千美元的奖励。这就产生了一些奇怪的激励措施，未成年人因为注册了最初伤害他们的平台而获得奖励。

children.author: 59percentmore
children.textRawHtml:
The point of a fine is to change behavior. It's not outsize if it's enough to do that.

>If this fine remains, and Meta pays out to the affected parties, these kids could end up rewarded with thousands of dollars for just for having a Facebook or Instagram account.

Good. https://www.thefader.com/2015/12/03/on-fleek-peaches-monroee...

These platforms are so profitable precisely because they fleece users for way more value vis a vis their data than they get back in service utility. Balancing that equation is the right thing to do.
children.textZhHtml:
罚款的目的是改变行为。如果足以做到这一点的话，这并不算过分。

>如果罚款仍然存在，并且 Meta 向受影响的各方支付费用，这些孩子最终可能会因为拥有 Facebook 或 Instagram 帐户而获得数千美元的奖励。

很好。 https://www.thefader.com/2015/12/03/on-fleek-peaches-monroee...

这些平台之所以如此有利可图，正是因为它们从用户的数据中获取的价值远高于他们在服务效用中获得的价值。平衡这个等式是正确的做法。

children.author: cheschire
children.textRawHtml: I feel like you skipped the next sentence from GP. This type of award might not balance the equation the way you think it does.
children.textZhHtml: 我觉得你跳过了 GP 的下一句话。此类奖励可能不会像您想象的那样平衡。

children.author: DiscourseFan
children.textRawHtml: Yes but Meta is being rewarded for harming children currently. So you're arguing, in fact, that we should not give kids money as restitution because it would create a bad "incentive" for them, rather than disincentivize the company that has already brought them harm from further harming them?
children.textZhHtml: 是的，但 Meta 目前因伤害儿童而受到奖励。所以你实际上是在争论，我们不应该给孩子钱作为赔偿，因为这会给他们带来不良的“激励”，而不是阻止已经给他们带来伤害的公司进一步伤害他们？

children.author: munk-a
children.textRawHtml: If this ruling results in Meta fully withdrawing from New Mexico because it's unlikely they'll actually net on a per customer basis than nothing of value will be lost.
children.textZhHtml: 如果这一裁决导致 Meta 完全退出新墨西哥州，因为他们不太可能真正从每个客户的基础上获利，那么任何有价值的东西都不会丢失。

children.author: 59percentmore
children.textRawHtml:
I understand now that this line

>and Meta pays out to the affected parties

probably won't come to pass, which I agree is not nearly as good. But I was responding to that possibility, as put forward by the the parent.
children.textZhHtml:
我现在明白，这条线

>和 Meta 向受影响方支付的费用

可能不会实现，我同意这不太好。但我是在回应家长提出的这种可能性。

children.author: Petersipoi
children.textRawHtml:
The line you conveniently skipped is

> Which creates some bizarre incentives
children.textZhHtml:
您方便地跳过的那一行是

>，这会产生一些奇怪的激励

children.author: abustamam
children.textRawHtml: The status quo is already bizarre. Meta is actively profiting from harming minors. The alternative (minors getting a payout by visiting harmful websites) seems pretty tame by contrast, and in fact puts an active incentive on Meta to stop letting minors be harmed by their software.
children.textZhHtml: 现状已经很奇怪了。 Meta 正在积极地通过伤害未成年人来获利。相比之下，另一种选择（未成年人通过访问有害网站获得报酬）似乎相当温和，事实上，它对 Meta 提供了积极的激励，以阻止未成年人受到其软件的伤害。

children.author: eastbound
children.textRawHtml:
One would argue the kids got paid for finding a dangerous place and entering. Up to the building owner to prevent access. It’s a form of giant bug bounty.

I wish I’d be paid a 7k$ bounty for every website where I can find an underage vulnerability.
children.textZhHtml:
有人会说，孩子们因为找到危险的地方并进入而获得了报酬。由建筑物业主决定阻止访问。这是巨额漏洞赏金的一种形式。

我希望每一个我能找到未成年漏洞的网站都能获得 7k 美元的赏金。

children.author: ktallett
children.textRawHtml: The key thing is these people will get older and no longer be in that age bracket so you are relying on future groups in that age bracket to know this loophole which will be some but far fewer I suspect.
children.textZhHtml: 关键是这些人会变老，不再处于那个年龄段，所以你需要依靠那个年龄段的未来群体来了解这个漏洞，我怀疑这个漏洞会有所增加，但要少得多。

children.author: shermantanktop
children.textRawHtml:
The inverse incentive is what's in place today: a platform actively harming the users who signed up for it, in pursuit of ad dollars. The incentive is to extract maximum revenue while disregarding the real-world effects of actions, including driving children to self-harm or mental illness.

That's bizarre. But I know for some people, it doesn't seem bizarre, and just seems like "capitalism."
children.textZhHtml:
反向激励就是当今的情况：一个平台为了追求广告收入而主动伤害注册它的用户。 其动机是获取最大收入，同时忽视行为对现实世界的影响，包括导致儿童自残或患精神疾病。

这很奇怪。 但我知道对于某些人来说，这并不奇怪，只是看起来像“资本主义”。

children.author: philipallstar
children.textRawHtml: The platform isn't actively harming. It's actively driving them to content they engage with. What they're choosing to engage with is harmful. The fact their parents let them on the platform is the crazy part, but the state already extracts vast amounts of money from them.
children.textZhHtml: 该平台并未主动造成伤害。它积极地推动他们接触他们感兴趣的内容。他们选择参与的事情是有害的。事实上，他们的父母让他们进入这个平台，这才是疯狂的部分，但国家已经从他们身上榨取了大量金钱。

children.author: 59percentmore
children.textRawHtml: I just saw an ad for Instagram's teen features, aimed at parents. You can't advertise for your product and then say that people are using it of their own volition. We are right back to the 90s and Big Tobacco.
children.textZhHtml: 我刚刚看到一则针对家长的 Instagram 青少年功能广告。你不能为你的产品做广告，然后说人们是自愿使用它的。我们又回到了 90 年代和大烟草公司。

children.author: lostlogin
children.textRawHtml:
Governments regulate all sorts of things that could be handled by the parents. However it works better setting a standard via regulation.

The world is moving to regulate these companies due to the harm they are causing.
children.textZhHtml:
政府对父母可以处理的各种事情进行监管。然而，通过监管制定标准效果更好。

由于这些公司造成的危害，世界正在开始对其进行监管。

children.author: mlsu
children.textRawHtml: Why punish S.E. Massengill? It’s the parents, after all, who willingly allowed their children to drink sulfanilamide. Hell, if the children simply closed their mouths when the spoon is in front of them, they’d be perfectly fine!
children.textZhHtml: 为什么要惩罚 S.E.马森吉尔？毕竟，是父母心甘情愿地让孩子喝磺胺。天哪，如果孩子们在勺子在他们面前时闭上嘴，他们就没事了！

children.author: philipallstar
children.textRawHtml: This is a silly comparison. Social media doesn't instantly kill your children, and we've known it's bad for them for ages now so parents have had time to adjust. Give kids devices, win stupid prizes.
children.textZhHtml: 这是一个愚蠢的比较。社交媒体不会立即杀死你的孩子，而且我们很早就知道这对他们不好，所以父母有时间进行调整。给孩子们设备，赢得愚蠢的奖品。

children.author: bluefirebrand
children.textRawHtml:
> The platform isn't actively harming.

> It's actively driving them to content they engage with

Regardless of whether or not that content is harmful or not
children.textZhHtml:
> 该平台并没有主动造成伤害。

> 它正在主动促使他们接触他们所参与的内容

无论该内容是否有害

children.author: gopher_space
children.textRawHtml: Lots of hidden variables in this equation, like the number of ex-parents living only for retribution.
children.textZhHtml: 这个方程中有很多隐藏变量，比如有多少前父母只是为了报应而活着。
